name: Landmine Meadows Row with Pause
description: The paused Meadows row adds a 2-3 second contraction hold at the peak of each repetition, maximizing lat and teres major activation at their shortest position. The pause eliminates the momentum that can occur in standard Meadows rows while training the ability to generate force from an already-contracted position — a quality associated with improved mind-muscle connection.

execution.starting_position: Barbell end secured in a landmine unit or corner. Staggered stance perpendicular to the bar. Hinge at the hips, grasp the bar end with one hand.
execution.setup_instructions: Reduce load by 20-30% compared to standard Meadows rows to accommodate the pause.
steps: Step 1: Row the bar end explosively to the hip.
Step 2: At the peak position, hold for 2-3 seconds with elbow above torso.
Step 3: During the hold, actively squeeze the lat — think 'armpit to hip'.
Step 4: Lower slowly under full control.
Step 5: Allow full lat stretch at the bottom before initiating the next rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row. Hold breath lightly during the pause. Exhale through the descent.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow drop during the pause — maintain height
Using the same load as standard Meadows rows — reduce weight for the pause variation
safety_considerations: Secure the barbell end before loading
Maintain braced core during the full range
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to elbow above torso with 2-3s hold.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the armpit at the top
Elbow stays high during the entire pause
Full stretch at the bottom before each rep
